briefdescription.para: A type expression is used to specify an abstract data type.

detaileddescription.para: In its compiled form, there are many different possible representations of an abstract data type, depending on how it is declared, and depending on how it is used. A TypeExpression may be used to indicate either a Constant (such as a ModuleConstant, PackageConstant, ClassConstant, etc.) or a TypeConstant (such as a ClassTypeConstant, a ParameterTypeConstant, etc.) Often, a type expression must provide a compiled representation of itself before it is able to resolve what its actual ADT will be; in these cases, the type expression can create a temporary place-holder, known as an unresolved constant, which will later be replaced with the real ADT information once the type information has been fully resolved.
